description: Maya is organizing a box of roughly 300 family photo negatives into a keepsake archive for her grandmother's ninetieth birthday. She must make the final call about the selection, digital format, privacy settings, and preservation plan after hearing from four relatives.

agents.name: Maya
agents.role: Family Archive Keeper and Final Decision-Maker

shared_context.S1: The family has about 300 35mm negatives from several decades of family gatherings and vacations.
shared_context.S2: Maya is assembling a keepsake archive for their grandmother's ninetieth birthday.
shared_context.S3: The archive can include a printed album, digital copies for relatives, and preserved original negatives.
shared_context.S4: Maya's usual family-project routine is to give each person a turn to raise practical or personal concerns before she locks the plan.
shared_context.S5: The family wants the finished archive ready before the birthday celebration in October.

PF1.text: Leo has a handwritten note from their grandmother asking for exactly 40 photographs in the printed album and saying that the images should stay in a private family collection rather than being posted publicly; he has not shown the note to Maya.

PF2.text: Nina has low vision and needs the digital companion copy to use 16-point high-contrast captions and layout to read it comfortably; she has not raised this requirement with Maya.

PF3.text: Omar spoke with a family photographer, Carla Mendes, who recommended scanning the negatives at exactly 6000 dpi as TIFF masters and storing the originals in acid-free sleeves; Carla's recommendation has not reached the group.

PF4.text: Tessa was told by their cousin Daniel, who appears in several photographs, that six negatives showing Daniel's children must not be included in either the printed album or the digital folder; Daniel's request has not been shared with Maya.

acceptance_conditions: The printed album must contain exactly 40 photographs.
The digital and printed archive must be restricted to named family members rather than posted publicly.
The digital companion copy must use 16-point high-contrast captions and layout.
The scanning plan must create exactly 6000 dpi TIFF master files.
Exactly six negatives must be excluded because they show Daniel's children.
A commitment to store the original negatives in acid-free sleeves must be recorded.
Daniel's request about excluding the six negatives must be cited as justification after it is spoken aloud.

content_checks.C2: decisions['sharing_scope'] == 'private family collection only, no public posting' or any(c['type'] == 'sharing_scope' or c['type'] == 'sharing_restriction' or c['type'] == 'privacy' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C3: decisions['digital_format'] == '16pt_high_contrast' or any(c['type'] == 'accessibility' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C4: decisions['scan_master_format'] == '6000dpi_tiff' or any(c['type'] == 'scan_spec' or c['type'] == 'scanning_spec' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'acid_free_storage' or c['type'] == 'preservation' or c['type'] == 'scan_spec' or c['type'] == 'scanning_spec' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The grandmother's note changes the album quantity from an open selection to exactly 40 photographs and changes sharing from a generic digital distribution to named family members only.
Nina's low vision changes the digital format from ordinary captions and layout to exactly 16-point high-contrast captions and layout.
Carla's recommendation changes the scan setting to exactly 6000 dpi TIFF masters and changes storage from an unspecified method to acid-free sleeves.
Daniel's request changes the exclusion count from an open editing choice to exactly six negatives and supplies the specific private fact that must be cited after Tessa speaks.
